piece_type: Instagram reel (company account + paid celebrity influencer partnership)

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Risk information presented only at the end of the reel, after Nate Berkus says, “see you guys at the next big event” and the screen goes black; after ~3 seconds of black screen, risk information appears as onscreen text using fast-paced, scrolling font that is small and difficult to read.
cases.context: Indication shown as static text throughout ~40 s presentation; scroll speed ~2,640-5,184 wpm vs ~238 wpm average reading; 'Swipe left for Important Consumer Safety Information' leads to no risk info; caption risk info requires scrolling.
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with prominence/readability comparable to benefits; minimizes boxed-warning risks.
cases.check: Rule: compute on-screen risk text reading speed (words / seconds on screen); flag if far above ~240 wpm, or if risk follows a black screen/end card.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “Keeping my dermatologist on speed dial is my secret weapon for looking fresh. You never know when those lines might decide to make a surprise appearance. That’s why she recommended Xeomin . . . that smooths the look of frown lines . . . .” | caption: “My pro-tips for getting ready for a night out; tuxedo at the ready, fries and Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) @xeominaesthetic for smoothing my frown lines”
cases.context: Same-day 'big night out' framing; primary endpoint at Day 30; composite success not evaluated before Day 7.
cases.check: Does the narrative timeline (same-day event) imply onset faster than the label's demonstrated time to effect?

cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “a double-filtered smart tox that smooths the looks of frown lines with only the ingredients that you need for treatment” | “#SmartTox”
cases.context: No head-to-head studies vs other botulinum toxins; PI notes neurotoxin 'without accessory proteins'.
cases.rationale: Implies manufacturing/formulation confers benefits over other botulinum toxin products.
cases.check: Do formulation or manufacturing descriptors ('smart', 'pure', 'only what you need') imply clinical advantage over competitors without head-to-head data?
